class.name: NNBTNodes
class.brief_description: Base class for all Noodle Nodes behaviour tree nodes.
class.description: Behaviour Trees are a commonly used structure that can be used to create artificial intelligence in games for the non-playable characters. A behaviour tree has a root node and under it a tree structure, where the branches of the tree define the behaviour for the AI. The utility enabled Behaviour Trees in Noodle Nodes GDExtension extend the traditional Behaviour Tree with utility functions. The Behaviour Tree nodes can be used as a regular behaviour tree, but the extended utility features allow you to add utility-based branch selection and execution of the Node Query System queries within your trees. The Behaviour Tree in Noodle Nodes GDExtension allows you to tick the tree by giving blackboard as input. This blackboard can be a dictionary that you want to use as the blackboard or the AI actor node itself. Or any other type of Variant. Or just null. The typed [NNBlackboard] resource on the nearest [NNBTRoot] ancestor is authoritative for [method get_blackboard_resource], [method get_blackboard], [method set_blackboard], [method has_blackboard], [method erase_blackboard] and [method get_actor]. The [Variant] passed to [method NNBTRoot.tick] remains legacy user data / actor and is never consulted by these helpers. With no [NNBTRoot] ancestor the helpers return their default value, [code]false[/code] or [code]null[/code] without reporting errors. [NNBTNodeReference] resolves these helpers from its target's own position in the tree. Each node tracks a run lifecycle. A run starts with the [code]on_before_run[/code] hook the first time the node is ticked while no run is active, and it ends with either the [code]on_after_run[/code] hook (when the node returns [code]SUCCESS[/code] or [code]FAILURE[/code]) or the [code]on_interrupt[/code] hook (when the active run is abandoned). Every [code]on_before_run[/code] is matched by exactly one [code]on_after_run[/code] or [code]on_interrupt[/code] for the same run, and a node that never started a run receives no lifecycle callback. The [code]on_before_run[/code], [code]on_after_run[/code] and [code]on_interrupt[/code] script hooks are provided by [NNBTTaskNodes]; composite nodes participate in the run lifecycle internally only. The [code]SKIP[/code] result is not terminal: the run stays active until it completes or is interrupted. [method interrupt] is idempotent and does nothing when the node has no active run. Disabling a node interrupts and resets its subtree, so re-enabling the node starts a fresh run on the next tick.

method.name: erase_blackboard
method.description: Erases [param key] from the blackboard of the nearest [NNBTRoot] ancestor. Returns [code]false[/code] when the key is absent or when there is no root.

method.name: get_actor
method.description: Returns the actor resolved by the nearest [NNBTRoot] ancestor, or [code]null[/code] when there is no root.

method.name: get_blackboard
method.description: Returns the value stored under [param key] in the blackboard of the nearest [NNBTRoot] ancestor. Returns [param default_value] when the key is missing, its value is [code]null[/code], or there is no root.

method.name: get_blackboard_resource
method.description: Returns the effective [NNBlackboard] of the nearest [NNBTRoot] ancestor: the board explicitly assigned to that root, or the root's own private board when none is assigned. Returns [code]null[/code] only when there is no [NNBTRoot] ancestor.

method.name: get_tree_root
method.description: Returns a relative node path to the furthest direct [NNBTNodes] ancestor.

method.name: has_blackboard
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] when [param key] exists in the blackboard of the nearest [NNBTRoot] ancestor and its value is not [code]null[/code]; returns [code]false[/code] otherwise, including when there is no root.

method.name: set_blackboard
method.description: Stores [param value] under [param key] in the blackboard of the nearest [NNBTRoot] ancestor. Returns [code]false[/code] when the key is empty or there is no root.

method.name: interrupt
method.description: Force-stops the node's active run. Task nodes run their [code]on_interrupt[/code] script hook and every still-active behaviour tree child is interrupted as well. Calling it on a node without an active run is a safe no-op, so it is idempotent.

members.member: Used with Utility-based Behaviour Tree nodes. This defines how the [NNConsideration] nodes (assigned as child nodes of the behaviour tree node) are evaluated to calculate the score for the node. The default is [code]Multiply[/code] (4). In GDScript use the class constants, for example [code]NNBTNodes.Multiply[/code]. The enum-scoped form [code]NNBTNodes.NNBTNodesEvaluationMethod.Multiply[/code] is also accepted; there is no bare global enum name.
The current internal status of the node, useful for debugging and seeing how the execution progresses. The following choices are possible: "Unticked:0,Ticked:1,Completed:2".

Defines how the Behaviour Tree node is reset. The default is [code]WHEN_TICKED_AFTER_BEING_COMPLETED[/code] (2). In GDScript use the class constants, for example [code]NNBTNodes.WHEN_TICKED[/code]. The enum-scoped form [code]NNBTNodes.NNBTNodesResetRule.WHEN_TICKED[/code] is also accepted; there is no bare global enum name.
The score this node received from the Utility-based evaluation.

constants.constant: Resets the node at the start of every tick, so it replays from its first child.
Resets the node as soon as it completes, so the next tick starts a fresh run.
Resets the node on the first tick after it has completed, which is the default.
Adds the scores of the enabled considerations.
Uses the lowest score of the enabled considerations.
Uses the highest score of the enabled considerations.
Uses the average score of the enabled considerations.
Multiplies the scores of the enabled considerations, which is the default.
Uses the first score greater than zero, ignoring considerations that score zero.
